milestones.title: Regency seat moved to the Great Post Road
milestones.detail: Governor-General Daendels ordered the chief settlement of Bandung moved from Krapyak, about ten kilometres south, to the point where the new Great Post Road crosses the Cikapundung river. The city dates its founding to 25 September 1810.
milestones.source: S.A. Reitsma, 'Bandoeng: voorheen, thans en in de toekomst', Tropisch Nederland (March 1933), abridged and reprinted by Java Post, https://javapost.nl/2011/10/26/bandoeng-een-stad-met-toekomst/ ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bandung

milestones.title: First Grand Mosque built on the town square
milestones.detail: The regent laid out the alun-alun with his residence and a mosque. The first mosque was a simple wooden building with a thatched roof.

milestones.title: Bandung becomes seat of the Preanger Resident
milestones.detail: The Dutch Resident of the Preanger Regencies moved his seat from Cianjur to Bandung. English Wikipedia's History of Bandung dates the decision to 1850.
milestones.source: S.A. Reitsma, 'Bandoeng: voorheen, thans en in de toekomst', Tropisch Nederland (March 1933), abridged and reprinted by Java Post, https://javapost.nl/2011/10/26/bandoeng-een-stad-met-toekomst/

milestones.title: State Railway reaches Bandung
milestones.detail: The state railway from Batavia via Buitenzorg opened to Bandung in 1884 and the railway workshops were set up in the town.
milestones.source: S.A. Reitsma, 'Bandoeng: voorheen, thans en in de toekomst', Tropisch Nederland (March 1933), abridged and reprinted by Java Post, https://javapost.nl/2011/10/26/bandoeng-een-stad-met-toekomst/

milestones.title: Bandung becomes a municipality
milestones.detail: A municipal council was installed on 1 April 1906. The municipal area was 19.22 square kilometres.
milestones.source: S.A. Reitsma, 'Bandoeng: voorheen, thans en in de toekomst', Tropisch Nederland (March 1933), abridged and reprinted by Java Post, https://javapost.nl/2011/10/26/bandoeng-een-stad-met-toekomst/ ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bandung

milestones.title: Technical college opens; Gedung Sate begun
milestones.detail: The Technische Hoogeschool (now Institut Teknologi Bandung) opened in 1920, and construction of the government offices known as Gedung Sate began on 27 July 1920 as departments moved from Batavia. Gedung Sate was completed in September 1924.
milestones.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gedung_Sate ; Statesman's Year-Book 1921, p. 1114 (Technical High School at Bandoeng erected in 1920), https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Page:Statesman%27s_Year-Book_1921.djvu/1166

milestones.title: Garden-city framework plan approved
milestones.detail: Bandung adopted a framework plan covering 12,758 hectares, applied mainly in the northern, largely European part of town.
milestones.source: Cor Passchier, Bandung: A short history on urban and architectural development, https://www.pac-nl.org/downloads/bandungashorthostorycp08.pdf , via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Bandung

milestones.title: Bandung Sea of Fire
milestones.detail: On 24 March 1946 withdrawing Indonesian forces deliberately set much of southern Bandung alight rather than hand it over after a British ultimatum.

milestones.title: Asian-African Conference
milestones.detail: Leaders of twenty-nine Asian and African countries met at Gedung Merdeka for the Bandung Conference.

milestones.title: City boundary expanded to about 167 sq km
milestones.detail: Under the Greater Bandung plan the city area, 19.22 square kilometres in 1906, reached 167.2965 square kilometres.
milestones.source: Bandung Dalam Angka 2003 (Bureau of Statistics), via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bandung

milestones.title: Cipularang toll road and Pasupati Bridge open
milestones.detail: The Cipularang toll road to Jakarta was completed in May 2005 and the cable-stayed Pasupati Bridge across the Cikapundung valley on 25 June 2005.

milestones.title: Al-Jabbar Grand Mosque completed in Gedebage
milestones.detail: The provincial grand mosque on the city's eastern edge was completed on 30 December 2022.

The CTBUH page says the 92 m height 'is estimated, based on a floor count of 27 floors'; no measured height was found. Completion in 2018 is as CTBUH lists it. notes: Start date: Bandung is a young city. The present site was settled when the seat of the Bandung regency was moved from Krapyak to the Great Post Road in 1810 (decree of 25 May 1810 quoted by Reitsma; the city's official anniversary is 25 September 1810). English Wikipedia says the earliest reference to the Bandung area dates to 1488, but that concerns the region, not the town, so 1810 is used and is not seriously contested. Population: the series is thin and has no point before 1846. The 1846-1933 points are rounded figures quoted in two Dutch texts by or after Mayor S.A. Reitsma (1921 and 1933), not census tables, and they do not share one boundary: the 1905 census figure ('not quite 48,000') is higher than the 38,000 Passchier gives for the municipality created in 1906, and the Statesman's Year-Book figure for 1918 (58,649) is far below the 102,000 quoted for 1920. The original 1920 and 1930 census volumes could not be reached, so there is no 1930 census point; the closest figure is 'over 160,000' on 1 January 1933. English Wikipedia also quotes 'about 12,000 inhabitants around 1850', consistent with the 1846 count. The 1949 figure (590,000) is a rounded secondary figure. Chandler has no pre-1950 entry for Bandung. Landmarks: this list is weak before 1988. No sourced height was found for the colonial-era buildings that define the city (Gedung Sate, 1924; Villa Isola, 1933; Gedung Merdeka; St Peter's Cathedral; Hotel Savoy Homann), for the Pasupati Bridge pylon or for the Bandung Lautan Api monument (Indonesian Wikipedia gives 45 m but no completion year), so they are omitted. Two taller towers listed by CTBUH (Galeri Ciumbuleuit 2, 116 m; Tamansari Panoramic Tower 1, 115 m) are omitted because CTBUH gives no completion year. Milestone dates for the railway (1884 here, 1880 on English Wikipedia) and the Resident's move (1862 here, 1850 on English Wikipedia) differ between sources; the dates used are those in Reitsma's 1933 article.
